### Overall plan

According to ChatGPT, we will need multiple CMS datasets: 
1. "Hospital General Information": This gives information on hospital name, location, type, overall rating, etc.
2. "Complications & Deaths": This gives mortality based on disease
3. "Unplanned Hospital Visits": This gives readmissions based on disease

It said that these datasets are "essential". It listed 3 more datasets, but not as essential. For now, I'll just try with these 3.

Next we create a function to retrieve the data. (Maybe this counts as functional programming?). The Provider Data Catalog allows for API access without an API key. (what does that mean??)

```{r}
get_cms_data <- function(dataset_id, limit = 1000) {

  url <- paste0(
    "https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/api/1/",
    "datastore/query/",
    dataset_id,
    "/0"
  )

  response <- request(url) |>
    req_url_query(
      limit = limit,
      offset = 0
    ) |>
    req_perform()

  result <- resp_body_json(
    response,
    simplifyVector = TRUE
  )

  as_tibble(result$results) |>
    clean_names()
}

#Now we actually call the function using the dataset IDs. Then we put the outputs into dataframes

hospitals <- get_cms_data("xubh-q36u")
dim(hospitals)
glimpse(hospitals)

complications_deaths <- get_cms_data("ynj2-r877")
dim(complications_deaths)
glimpse(complications_deaths)

# I think it works now. 
unplanned_readmissions <- get_cms_data("632h-zaca")
dim(unplanned_readmissions)
glimpse(unplanned_readmissions)
```

```{r}
library(httr2)

url <- paste0(
  "https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/api/1/",
  "datastore/query/632h-zaca/0"
)

response <- request(url) |>
  req_url_query(
    limit = 10,
    offset = 0
  ) |>
  req_headers(Accept = "application/json") |>
  req_error(is_error = function(resp) FALSE) |>
  req_perform()

resp_status(response)

resp_body_string(response)
```

```{r}
# storing the data
## working directory needs to be set first
write_csv(hospitals, "data/hospitals_2026-11-11.csv")
write_csv(complications_deaths, "data/complications_deaths_2026-11-11.csv")
write_csv(unplanned_readmissions, "data/unplanned_readmissions_2026-11-11.csv")
```
